extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: A context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for large multimodal model evaluation, covering eight real-world scenarios (time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes) with human-written instruction-response pairs.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from multiple sources: LAION-5B via keyword search using CLIP-retrieval UI for Time, Shopping, Navigation & Abstract categories; Rico Dataset for Application Usage; web scraping of Open WebText Initiative links for Web Usage; and test sets of existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA, STVQA, ESTVQA) for Infographic and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes categories. Each sample was annotated with novel instruction-response pairs following collection guidelines requiring context-sensitive reasoning over text and visual elements.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from LAION-5B (retrieved via CLIP-retrieval UI with keyword search), Rico Dataset (66,000 distinct UI screens from 9,300 Android apps), screenshots from Open WebText Initiative website links, and test set images from InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Authors divided into two groups annotated instruction-response pairs following strict annotation guidelines. MTurk workers verified correctness of each sample. Each author group reviewed samples created by the other group to ensure guideline adherence and filter low-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) for verification stage
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 96% of samples were found to be annotated correctly by MTurk verifiers; incorrect samples were filtered out
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR used for heuristic-based filtering to detect text in images and select top 500 images with highest word count
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human annotators for the baseline were mainly from the US, introducing potential linguistic and cultural bias. The linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses would change with different social groups.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains only 506 instances, which may limit generalizability. Human baseline was established mainly with US-based annotators, limiting diversity. The dataset focuses on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning and is not suitable for evaluating basic OCR capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to evaluate LMMs on real-world tasks such as navigating public spaces and assisting the visually impaired. The authors ensured images and instructions are not offensive to any social group, and noted that model responses may hallucinate but no apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information was observed.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating (benchmarking) the context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models. It covers eight real-world visual scenarios and supports both zero-shot and few-shot evaluation settings.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code, and a continuously updated leaderboard are made publicly available. The leaderboard is updated with recent LMMs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were filtered using manual filtering (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract categories) or heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR (for Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, Miscellaneous Natural Scenes), selecting top 500 images with highest word count. Incorrect samples (4%) were filtered out after MTurk verification, and cross-group author review filtered low-quality samples, resulting in 506 final instances.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images sourced from LAION-5B via keyword search using CLIP-retrieval UI with category-specific keywords. Images from Rico Dataset, Open WebText Initiative screenshots, and existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA, STVQA, ESTVQA) were reannotated with novel instruction-response pairs. Manual and heuristic-based filtering applied to ensure suitability for annotation, followed by a three-stage annotation process including author annotation and MTurk verification.

name.evidence: we introduce CONTEXTUAL, a novel dataset featuring human-crafted instructions that require context-sensitive reasoning for text-rich images.

description.evidence: we propose CONTEXTUAL, a Context-sensitive Text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for LMMs evaluation. CONTEXTUAL covers eight real-world scenarios with text-rich images: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes

rai:dataCollection.evidence: CONTEXTUAL comprises images sourced from six different sources. Firstly, we obtain images for the Time, Shopping, Navigation & Abstract categories from the LAION-5B... Secondly, we source images for the Application Usage category from the Rico Dataset... Thirdly, we scrape the website links made available by the Open WebText Initiative... Lastly, we acquire images from the test sets of existing VQA datasets

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We divide the authors into two groups, namely Group 1 and Group 2, each responsible for annotating four specific categories. The authors strictly adhered to the provided annotation guidelines throughout the annotation. We asked MTurk workers (mutually exclusive from the ones used for human performance baseline and human evaluation) to verify the correctness of each sample <image, instruction, response> and found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We asked MTurk workers (mutually exclusive from the ones used for human performance baseline and human evaluation) to verify the correctness of each sample

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. Filtering out the incorrect samples, we tasked each author group to review the samples created by the other group.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we employ a PaddleOCR (paddlepadle, 2023) to detect the text in the image. Subsequently, we select the top 500 images with the highest number of words

rai:dataBiases.evidence: In our experiments, we asked human annotators, mainly from the US, to provide responses to establish a human baseline. We are aware that the linguistic diversity and writing style of the human responses would change with different social groups.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The extension of our work can focus on understanding the impact of different social groups on the human baseline performance on the CONTEXTUAL dataset. A similar argument is relevant for human evaluation of the model responses. To obtain more reliable human evaluation results, future work would involve annotators from more diverse regions.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: During our data collection, we aim to ensure that the images, human-written instructions, and reference responses are not offensive to any social group. We are aware that the existing multimodal models are capable of generating harmful responses, despite the presence of safeguard filter. In addition, our qualitative analysis reveals that the model responses would hallucinate, however, we did not observe any apparent harmful and privacy sensitive information in them.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: CONTEXTUAL is proposed to evaluate the context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models... We conduct experiments to assess the performance of 14 foundation models (GPT-4V, Gemini-Pro-Vision, LLaVA-Next) and establish a human performance baseline.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We make the dataset and code available to the LMM community along with a continuously updated leaderboard with recent LMMs.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: we employ a PaddleOCR to detect the text in the image. Subsequently, we select the top 500 images with the highest number of words... Filtering out the incorrect samples, we tasked each author group to review the samples created by the other group... we end up with a dataset of 506 instances.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we use keyword search using CLIP-retrieval UI... we scrape the website links made available by the Open WebText Initiative... we reannotate these image instances, categorizing them into two groups: Infographic, sourced from the InfographicVQA dataset, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, sourced from the STVQA and ESTVQA datasets.
